tolerances_note:
tol = max(1e-6, B rounded up to 2 significant figures), B = (2*kappa*G1 + c0)*u, u = 2^-24. Real path: kappa = sqrt(2), G1 = 9n, c0 = 1. Complex path: kappa = 2*sqrt(2) + 1, G1 = 16n, c0 = 3. CNOT is an exact permutation. For a unit-norm observable |d

| <= 2*|d psi| + |d psi|^2. X/Y on cpu_compiled: EXLA float32 sum bounded by (2^(n-1) + 3)*u (Higham 2002, section 4.2). tolerance_formula below holds the inputs; test/nx_quantum/bench_tolerance_formula_test.exs recomputes every NxQuantum family and continuity tolerance from them. Timed mode refuses to run while tolerances_confirmed is false. The owner confirmation (R3: at least 1e-6 means tol >= 1e-6) and the physics seat sign-off flip it in a separate commit.

tolerance_formula.continuity_rule: one tolerance per scenario, shared by both NxQuantum lanes: the bound of the looser lane (cpu_compiled where X/Y observables run on EXLA)

real.structure: H on every wire; then for layer l in 0..L-1: RY(w, angle[l*n+w]) for w in 0..n-1, then CNOT(i,i+1) for i = l mod 2, l mod 2 + 2, ... while i+1 < n

complex.structure: for layer l in 0..L-1: RX(w, angle[l*2n+w]) for w in 0..n-1, RZ(w, angle[l*2n+n+w]) for w in 0..n-1, then CNOT(i,i+1) for i = l mod 2, l mod 2 + 2, ... while i+1 < n; no H layer

prefix_parity.real: RY(w, theta_w) on every wire, then CNOT(j,j+1) for j = 0..n-2 in ascending order; <Z_k> = prod_{j<=k} cos(theta_j)
prefix_parity.complex: RX(w, theta_w) then RZ(w, phi_w) on every wire, then the same CNOT chain; <Z_k> = prod_{j<=k} cos(theta_j)

disclosures.nxquantum: NxQuantum simulates in complex64 and returns float32 expectation values. Real-gate Pauli-Z circuits (H, X, Z, RY, CNOT) use a float64 state with float32-rounded gate coefficients. The ⟨Z⟩ sums accumulate in float64. Both `cpu_portable` and `cpu_compiled` evolve on Nx.BinaryBackend.
disclosures.qiskit: `qiskit.quantum_info.Statevector` simulates in complex128 and returns float64 expectation values.
disclosures.pennylane: `default.qubit` simulates in complex128 (its default for NumPy inputs) and returns float64 expectation values.
disclosures.cirq: `cirq.Simulator()` defaults to complex64. `simulate_expectation_values` renormalizes the final state using a norm computed by a single-precision BLAS dot, checks normalization with `np.isclose(norm, 1, atol=1e-7)` (which allows |norm − 1| ≤ 1.01e-5), and sums each expectation value in complex64 through NumPy/BLAS. It returns Python `complex` values, and the harness records their real part. On state-based scenarios its timed values are disclosed, not tolerance-checked; its sampled-counts rows (`cirq_c64`) are float64 Python helpers and are gated at 1e-6. Semantic equivalence is proven by an untimed run of the same circuit (identical gates and angles) with `cirq.Simulator(dtype=np.complex128)`. On this machine (Accelerate BLAS), the complex64 lane [<filled from the run>]; these are reported as measured, not extrapolated.
disclosures.cirq_placeholder: [<filled from the run>] must be replaced with the measured complex64 deviation before any Cirq row is published; the bracketed text is not a measurement.
methods: PennyLane is timed through `qml.execute` on a pre-built tape; no QNode.

agreement_note: Gated lanes end a check as pass or fail. cirq_c64 is ungated only on state-based scenarios (its complex64 state is disclosed, R5); its equivalence run cirq_c128_equivalence is gated at 1e-6 and decides whether a Cirq row is published. On sampled scenarios the Cirq and PennyLane rows are float64 Python helpers, so cirq_c64 is gated at 1e-6 there and publishable only when its own status is pass. A lane error counts as fail on a gated lane; for ungated cirq_c64 it is status error and the row is not publishable.
